# requireBoolean

<link-summary>Returns the value as a boolean, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireBoolean() — Returns the value as a boolean, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireBoolean(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a boolean."): boolean;
```

Only the two primitives pass. `new Boolean(false)` is an object, and the strings `"true"` and `"false"` are strings.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                        | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :----------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                          | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a boolean."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`boolean` — the same value, typed as a boolean.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                   |
| :------------------------- | :-------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a boolean. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireBoolean(true); // => true
requireBoolean(false); // => false
requireBoolean("true"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireBoolean(1); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
